content.text: Purpose
Create, update, and retire personas (Create / Update / Retire) — writes only produce drafts; the user decides on activation.

Conventions: Load only the sections of the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource this playbook needs — before Phase 2 (Propose), in one call: fetch_resource(resource_id, block_ids=["res-conv-h-modi", "res-conv-h-laengen", "res-conv-h-trigger"]). A heading anchor returns its whole section; the resource_id is in this playbook's links (linked_blocks). Load other sections only when needed (anchors via list_resource_blocks).
Trigger Keywords
new persona; new agent; create persona; edit persona; modify persona; change persona; retire persona; deactivate persona; retiring a persona.
Procedure

First identify the mode: Create, when the user names an agent/persona name that doesn't exist yet; Update, when they name an existing persona plus a change request; Retire, when they want to deactivate a persona. When ambiguous, first read get_persona(identifier) and clearly ask which persona is meant.

Create — Understand: Ask clarifying questions in phases, 1-2 per turn, never all at once. Identity (one concise line), Tone & Style (with example phrases), Allowed (4-6 concrete capabilities, no tool list), Forbidden (domain boundaries + anti-patterns), Output Style (form, length), Mode decision (actively check — criteria in the Modes section; as soon as multiple usage voices or output formats are needed, use Multi-Mode instead of a mixed persona).
Mode rule:
exactly one default mode (is_default=true, without trigger), every non-default mode with a mandatory trigger — details are binding in the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource, Mode Rule section.

Create — Propose: Consolidate the persona body (description + profile as Markdown with the sections Identity, Tone & Style, Allowed, Forbidden, Output Style; optional modes). Show it to the user, explain trade-offs, get confirmation.
Check length:

check the profile, every mode and the number of modes against the guide values in the Agent-Building Conventions (section 'Lengths & Placement', anchor res-conv-h-laengen). Procedures, checklists and tool instructions move into a playbook according to the placement table, schemas and reference knowledge into a resource; the profile keeps role, tone, a few rules with reasons and hard limits. If the draft is above the warning threshold, tell the user the word count and the guide value before you write.

Create — Write: Call create_persona(name, content) — only set locale explicitly if the persona is meant to deliberately deviate from the workspace language. The new version 1 is created server-side as status='draft' — never directly active. Set traits and tags for voice and domain respectively.

Update — Understand & Propose: Read get_persona(identifier), show the affected section (Identity / Tone & Style / Allowed / Forbidden / Output Style / Modes), clarify the change request, consolidate the edit proposal and have it confirmed.
Length on update:

the same check for the state after the change. If the profile or a mode grows above the warning threshold, propose moving content out. Shorten a persona that is already too long only if the user wants it.

Update — Write: Read the template with get_persona(identifier, format="source") — source Markdown with heading anchors and base_rev in the header. To change one field or section, use edit_content(entity_type, entity_id, base_rev, op, anchor | field, markdown), e.g. field='profile' or field='modes[<name>].identity_add'; the rest stays untouched. For a rework, call update_persona(persona_id, content) with the full state (profile and mode fields as Markdown). On an active version both create a new draft; if a draft is already open, update_persona returns 409, while edit_content writes into that draft when base_rev matches. Batch changes together instead of forcing a new version per micro-edit.

Links: Set which playbooks the persona should carry via set_persona_playbooks(persona_id, playbook_ids) (replace semantics — the list fully replaces the current state). First determine the right IDs with list_playbooks(). Relationship note: when wiring this up, check whether the linked playbooks themselves need resource links (set_playbook_resource_links, see the "Create & Maintain Playbook" playbook).
Activate: As soon as the user approves, call transition_persona(persona_id, version, to='active') — promoting is admin-gated and is the user's call. Never activate automatically on creation.

Retire: Read get_persona(identifier); check whether any agents use this persona, and warn the user. Then call transition_persona(persona_id, version, to='inactive'). restore_persona(persona_id, version) restores an earlier version as a new draft if a rollback is needed.
Modes (Multi-Mode Personas)
Set up modes as soon as the persona needs to serve
multiple usage voices or output formats

— e.g., concise chat support AND a detailed report, internal analysis AND a customer-facing answer. A single mixed persona dilutes both voices; separate personas duplicate the base identity. Modes solve this: one base identity, one overlay per mode.
Mandatory default:
exactly one mode carries is_default=true — it applies when no trigger keyword matches. Without a default mode, mode selection is undefined.
Trigger keywords:

every non-default mode needs concrete, comma-separated recognition keywords in the trigger field (e.g. 'report, summary, analysis') — this is how the consuming agent recognizes which mode matches the request. The default mode itself carries no trigger — it applies as a fallback and would otherwise collide with the non-default modes.
Fields per mode:

name, trigger, is_default, identity_add (addition to the base identity), output_style_override (replaces the base output style), and anti_patterns — the three content fields are each a Markdown document like the profile.

"modes": [
  {"name": "Chat", "trigger": "", "is_default": true,
   "identity_add": "Responds concisely and directly in a chat tone.",
   "output_style_override": "", "anti_patterns": ""},
  {"name": "Report", "trigger": "report, summary, analysis", "is_default": false,
   "identity_add": "",
   "output_style_override": "Structured Markdown report with subheadings.",
   "anti_patterns": ""}
]
Server-side retrieval:

Consuming agents call get_persona(identifier, mode='<mode-name>') — the server applies the mode to body_rendered (identity_add appends, output_style_override replaces the output style, anti_patterns apply additionally). Choose mode names and triggers concretely enough that matching from the user's request is unambiguous. Modes continue to be managed via update_persona (content.modes); individual mode fields can also be changed via edit_content (field='modes[<name>].<field>').
Pitfalls
transition_persona: draft/review requires persona_write, active/inactive requires promote_retire — without that right, activation stays with the user.
Don't activate on creation, and don't write to other aggregates through this playbook (playbooks, resources, and agents have their own playbooks).
Hand-Off
Have the user review the persona content and transition it to 'active' once approved.
Create matching playbooks (the Create & Maintain Playbook playbook) and link them via set_persona_playbooks.
Create an agent that carries this persona plus a system prompt template (the Create & Maintain Agent playbook).

For behavior-relevant updates: running sessions keep the old state cached — start a new chat for the new voice to take effect. For topics outside persona maintenance, politely redirect to the responsible playbook.
